digits_selection.description: Order a 100-point candidate pool of 8x8 handwritten digits (10 classes) for sequential selection; 100 validation and 1000 test points per instance (the paper's RQ3 large-dataset split).
digits_selection.notes: Results are the paper's Table 1 values (mean test accuracy and its +/- over 20 runs, OpenDataVal logistic regression). This gym uses the same split sizes and target model family, with class-balanced candidate pools and standardized features, so absolute accuracies run higher than the paper's (e.g. random ordering ~0.75 here vs 0.619); compare methods to the reproduced reference in scores_test.json, not to these numbers. The held-out test scores 100 hidden instances. Only random, loo, datashap and bipartite are implemented here; the other rows are the paper's.

mean_accuracy.description: Mean held-out test accuracy over the full selection curve (prefix sizes 1..100); the paper's Table 1 metric.

early10_accuracy.description: Mean test accuracy over prefix sizes 1..10 (10% of the pool): very-low-budget selection quality, where the paper reports the largest gaps.

early20_accuracy.description: Mean test accuracy over prefix sizes 1..20 (20% of the pool): early-selection sample efficiency.

tail_accuracy.description: Mean test accuracy over prefix sizes 21..100. Constraint side of the claim: early gains must not be bought by worse larger-budget prefixes.

max_accuracy_drop.description: Largest one-step decrease in test accuracy along the curve, averaged over instances (the paper's 'fewer fluctuations'); constraint metric.

curve_accuracy_std.description: Unscored. Standard deviation of test accuracy pooled over all prefix sizes and instances; reported because the paper's Table 1 '+/-' column is read as this quantity.

fried_selection.description: Order a 50-point candidate pool of the binarized Friedman #1 regression benchmark (OpenML 'fried', ID 901: 10 uniform features, target above its mean vs. not), regenerated from its published definition; 50 validation and 500 test points per instance (the paper's standard split).
fried_selection.notes: Results are the paper's Table 1 values for fried (mean test accuracy and +/- over 20 runs). The data are regenerated with sklearn.datasets.make_friedman1 (noise 1.0) and binarized at the sample mean as OpenML does, so they follow the same distribution as the OpenML table rather than being the identical 40768 rows. Replaces the earlier 'synthetic_planes' stand-in, which was near chance and did not reproduce the paper's direction. The held-out test scores 100 hidden instances. Only random, loo, datashap and bipartite are implemented here.

mean_accuracy.description: Mean held-out test accuracy over the full selection curve (prefix sizes 1..50); the paper's Table 1 metric.

early10_accuracy.description: Mean test accuracy over prefix sizes 1..10 (20% of the pool): very-low-budget selection quality, where the paper reports the largest gaps.

early20_accuracy.description: Mean test accuracy over prefix sizes 1..20 (40% of the pool): early-selection sample efficiency.

tail_accuracy.description: Mean test accuracy over prefix sizes 21..50. Constraint side of the claim: early gains must not be bought by worse larger-budget prefixes.

max_accuracy_drop.description: Largest one-step decrease in test accuracy along the curve, averaged over instances (the paper's 'fewer fluctuations'); constraint metric.

curve_accuracy_std.description: Unscored. Standard deviation of test accuracy pooled over all prefix sizes and instances; reported because the paper's Table 1 '+/-' column is read as this quantity.
